guidance.title: What scalp flakes can mean
guidance.text: An itchy, flaking scalp can occur with dandruff, but irritation and other skin conditions can look similar. The description alone cannot establish the cause.

guidance.title: What you can try
guidance.text: Regular washing may help mild dandruff. If it persists, dermatology guidance lists anti-dandruff shampoos with ingredients such as ketoconazole or salicylic acid. Follow the instructions on the package.

guidance.title: When to get checked
guidance.text: Ask a clinician if the scalp is very itchy, red or swollen, if flakes occur on other parts of the body, or if symptoms persist after about a month of anti-dandruff shampoo use.

guidance.title: Start with gentle skin care
guidance.text: Wash gently and avoid scrubbing or picking at breakouts. Harsh exfoliation can irritate skin. Choose a product meant for the area you are washing.

guidance.title: Ingredients discussed in acne guidance
guidance.text: Salicylic acid is an option for clogged pores such as whiteheads and blackheads. The acne guideline also discusses benzoyl peroxide. The right option depends on the kind of acne and how your skin responds.

guidance.title: When to see a dermatologist
guidance.text: Deep, painful spots or acne that is leaving scars are reasons to seek dermatology care.

guidance.title: The cause determines the options
guidance.text: Hair shedding and thinning can have different causes. A clinician may ask about the pattern, timing, illness, medicines and family history, then examine the scalp and decide whether tests are needed.

guidance.title: What you can do while getting assessed
guidance.text: Handle your hair gently and avoid hairstyles that pull tightly. Book a dermatology appointment to evaluate ongoing or unexplained hair loss.

guidance.title: An ingredient to discuss with a clinician
guidance.text: Topical minoxidil can help some people with early hair loss. Whether it is appropriate depends on the cause and your circumstances, so discuss it with a clinician before choosing a product.

ingredients.name: Minoxidil
ingredients.form: Topical scalp solution for discussion with a clinician

sources.title: Dermatologists' tips for relieving dry skin
How to pick the right moisturizer

guidance.title: Moisturize after washing
guidance.text: For ordinary dryness, take short, lukewarm showers and apply a fragrance-free cream or ointment while the skin is still damp.

guidance.title: What to look for on the label
guidance.text: Ceramides are one option in moisturizers that help the skin hold water. The rest of the formula matters, including its texture and whether it contains fragrance.

guidance.title: When to seek care
guidance.text: See a dermatologist if dryness continues despite skin care changes or creams routinely sting or burn. Very dry skin can also accompany other skin conditions.

ingredients.name: Ceramides
ingredients.form: Moisturizer. Check the full label for fragrance and other ingredients

title: Rough bumps on arms or legs

guidance.title: Rough bumps have several possible causes
guidance.text: A dermatologist can examine the bumps to confirm whether they are keratosis pilaris. Bumps on the arms or legs can have other causes, and similar-looking bumps may need different care.

guidance.title: What guidance discusses for confirmed keratosis pilaris
guidance.text: Moisturizing can help dryness. Dermatology guidance lists urea and lactic acid among ingredients that can improve rough texture. Exfoliating products can also irritate skin.

guidance.title: Three things to check on sunscreen labels
guidance.text: Look for SPF 30 or higher, broad-spectrum UVA and UVB protection, and water resistance. Check the complete package for all three.

guidance.title: Use more than one form of protection
guidance.text: Use shade and protective clothing alongside sunscreen. When outdoors, reapply sunscreen about every two hours and after swimming or sweating, following the product directions.

ingredients.name: Broad-spectrum sunscreen
ingredients.form: SPF label example. Confirm water resistance on the current package

guidance.title: Condition after washing
guidance.text: Apply shampoo mainly to the scalp. Conditioner helps moisturize and detangle the hair. For dry or curly hair, the AAD suggests using conditioner along its length.

guidance.title: Reduce heat and friction
guidance.text: Limit high heat from dryers, straighteners and curling irons. Blot wet hair gently rather than rubbing it with a towel.

ingredients.name: Hair conditioner
ingredients.form: Rinse-out hair care. Check the package for the full formula

guidance.title: What you can try for ordinary body odor
guidance.text: Wash and dry the areas that tend to sweat, and change clothes regularly. A deodorant can help with odor. If the main concern is how much you sweat, a pharmacist can advise on antiperspirants.

guidance.title: When to get checked
guidance.text: Ask a clinician about a sudden change in how much you sweat or how you smell, sweating at night, or sweating that affects daily activities.

ingredients.name: Deodorant
ingredients.form: Roll-on for odor. Check the label for antiperspirant status

sources.title: Sleep disorders and complementary health approaches
sources.publisher: NIH National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health

guidance.title: Start with a consistent sleep routine
guidance.text: Keep a regular wake time, wind down before bed, and limit evening caffeine. A dark and quiet room can make it easier to sleep.

guidance.title: When to seek care
guidance.text: Speak with a clinician if poor sleep has lasted for months, sleep habits have not helped, or the problem makes daily life hard. A clinician can discuss options such as cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia.

guidance.title: What the supplement evidence can tell you
guidance.text: Evidence for many sleep supplements is limited or inconsistent. Discuss any supplement with a clinician, especially if you take medicines. The current guide has no checked product match for treating insomnia.

guidance.title: Daily care that helps prevent cavities
guidance.text: Dental guidance recommends brushing with fluoride toothpaste and cleaning between teeth regularly. A dentist can tailor prevention advice to your risk of decay.

guidance.title: Why fluoride matters
guidance.text: Fluoride helps strengthen enamel and lower the risk of tooth decay. Check the ingredient label for fluoride before choosing a toothpaste for cavity prevention.

title: Dark spots and uneven skin tone

sources.title: How to fade dark spots in darker skin tones
Finding skin cancer in darker skin tones

guidance.title: Look at what preceded the mark
guidance.text: Dark marks can remain after a breakout or irritation heals. Finding and addressing the underlying cause helps guide what to do next.

guidance.title: Protect skin from sun and visible light
guidance.text: For dark spots in darker skin tones, dermatology guidance discusses tinted, broad-spectrum sunscreen with iron oxide, SPF 30 or higher, and water resistance.

guidance.title: Have new or changing spots checked
guidance.text: A new, changing, bleeding or otherwise unusual spot should be assessed by a dermatologist before using products to fade it.

ingredients.form: Tinted sunscreen. Check for broad-spectrum protection and water resistance

sources.title: Eating, diet and nutrition for constipation
sources.publisher: NIH National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

sources.title: Symptoms and causes of constipation
sources.publisher: NIH National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

guidance.title: Start with food and fluids
guidance.text: For uncomplicated constipation, guidance recommends eating fiber-rich foods, increasing fiber gradually, and drinking enough fluids to help fiber work. Whole grains, pulses, and fruit are common sources.

guidance.title: When to get medical care
guidance.text: Seek medical advice if constipation persists despite self-care. Get prompt care if you also have rectal bleeding, blood in your stool, ongoing abdominal pain, vomiting, or inability to pass gas.
